response.text:
The first attempt was rejected, most likely because of the account code format: the ledger stores ACCT_CD as an 8-character padded value. I sent '5500    ' with the padding, so that should have matched, and the amounts were sent as strings. The next most likely cause is how the check works. It probably sums DR_AMT on non-2000 lines for the journal and compares that to INV_AMT. My credit line sits in the CR column, so the DR sum stays at 1573.46 and the mismatch remains.

To make that DR sum equal 1537.46, I will correct the journal by netting the debit side. A debit of 1573.46 less 36.00 is only reachable with a credit if the check nets DR minus CR, so I'll send the correction as a credit line. The alternative is to add a debit, which would only raise the sum, so that is no use.

The correction needs the expense on journal 1406 to net to 1537.46 and the group to balance (DR 1537.46 = CR 1537.46). A credit of 36.00 to 5500 does this.

I'll resubmit that credit using the account code exactly as stored (padded) and numeric amounts.

arguments.reasoning: Journal 1406 debits expense 5500 for 1573.46 (digits transposed) while invoice 247 and the AP control credit are 1537.46. A one-sided 36.00 credit to 5500 in open period 11 nets the expense to 1537.46 and balances the original plus correction group. No invoice status change since this is not a duplicate.
